messages.subject: 1:1 nearest matching
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have a question regarding nearest matching method. my function is as
follows: m.out <- matchit(treat ~ SEX + ETHN + EDUC + log_VL_BL + CD4_BL +
Dur_HIV + hepC + hepB + IVD, data = mydata, method= "nearest")

Dur_HIV is the duration og HIV infection of a patient. How is a 1:1
matching done? I do not have 2 patients with the same duration of HIV
infection in days. Does it take the nearest duration? Also is the algorithm
atching 1:1 per variable or for all the variables?

Thanks,
Susan

-- 

Regards,
Susan Kamal

messages.subject: Re: 1:1 nearest matching
messages.body_plain:
Hi Susan,
Using the syntax below matchit will estimate a propensity score using all the variables you list in the model, and then will match subjects based on their propensity scores.  

If you want to match on each variable individually you could consider exact matching or coarsened exact matching (CEM).

Liz

messages.body_plain:
Dear list, 
I have a question
I have match using full match optional, this return also weights and subclass variables.
Must i in coxph function from survival package use also weights:
Coxph (....... ~ a + strata(subclass), weights= weights, data) or 
Coxph (....... ~ a + strata(subclass), data) or 
Coxph (....... ~ a , weights= weights, data) 

Thanks in advance
Sorry for noise
Meretrice Christmass
Inviato da iPad
